author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Grammy-winning rapper Lil Durk was acquitted Friday of all charges in a federal murder-for-hire trial in Los Angeles. The artist, whose legal name is Durk Banks, had been accused of ordering and financing a 2022 ambush intended to kill rival rapper Quando Rondo. The shooting instead killed Rondo’s cousin, Saviay’a Robinson, near the Beverly Center.

Prosecutors alleged that Banks sought retaliation for the 2020 killing of his friend and fellow rapper King Von. Defense lawyers argued that a former personal assistant arranged the plot without Banks’ knowledge. That former assistant and two other associates reached plea agreements and testified for the prosecution, according to the Los Angeles City News Service account cited by Reuters.

Two co-defendants tried with Banks were also acquitted of the central murder-for-hire charges but convicted of conspiracy to commit stalking and related stalking counts. Banks remains in custody despite Friday’s verdict because he faces a separate trial scheduled for October 5 on murder-related racketeering and weapons charges. He has pleaded not guilty in that case.
dek: The Grammy-winning rapper was cleared of all charges in the Los Angeles case but remains jailed ahead of a separate October trial.
headline: Lil Durk acquitted in federal murder-for-hire trial
